head: claude/mi106-manager-scope-authorship
title: manager-scope: authorship is a CLAIM — a mis-stamp now reads `unattributed`, not `violation` (MI-106)
body:
## Summary

`check_manager_scope.py` derived authorship from the `Claude-Session:` trailer — **which the author writes themselves**. This makes authorship a claim the guard can *contradict* from the lease register, adds the third state that was missing, and states the trailer's limits in the guard's own output so a mis-stamp reads as `unattributed` rather than as a graded verdict. MI-106.

⚠️ **The class is fixed; #10895 is not unblocked.** Those are different sentences and the registers said only the first — see *Filed for follow-ups*.

### The two bugs, one root

**The false positive, measured.** #10895 was blocked because `5504200c` touches `scripts/notify_on_pull.py` and `tests/test_notify_merge_pings.py` under a trailer naming `session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ` — the previous day's manager — so R2 read it as a manager doing an item. The register disagrees with the trailer: `MANAGER-LEASE.json`'s own history has that session releasing the lease at `2026-09-02T21:38:05Z`, and `session_01Nopk1HcpvWBSEbZxEmALkd` heartbeating at `06:06:14Z` and `06:35:44Z` — either side of the commit's `06:13:07Z` author time. The branch's own head commit (`7a93261f`) names the cause outright: the spawn dispatch handed the sub-session the **manager's** session URL to stamp. So the guard produced a **true** finding about what it could see and a **false** one about what happened.

**The dangerous half, unguarded.** A manager wanting to do an item could stamp a worker's session id and the guard vouched for it. The `unattributed` disclosure covered *untrailered* commits only; a *mis*-trailered one fell outside that caveat and rendered as graded. A guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard — the `new-table-wiring-guard` lesson its siblings already cite.

### What changed

`office_windows()` derives, from the git history of `MANAGER-LEASE.json`, the intervals in which each session actually **held** the lease. `attribute()` grades every commit into three states that do not collapse:

| state | meaning | graded? |
|---|---|---|
| `attributed` | trailer names a session the register independently places **in office** at the commit's author time | yes |
| `unattributed` | no trailer, **or** a trailer the register **contradicts** | no — reported loudly, and it now **dominates** `clean` |
| `not_manager` | trailer names a session that has never held the lease | R2 does not reach it |

This is not a workaround. R2's rule is *a **manager** commit touching a worker path*, and manager-ness is a property of a **moment**. A session that stood down yesterday is not the manager today, so grading its commits as management was wrong on the guard's own terms.

⚠️ **It contradicts; it never confirms — and the guard now says so on every verdict, including clean ones.** The register is evidence the commit's author cannot reach back and change, but the author date it is joined against is ordinary git metadata and is author-settable. This catches the **careless** mis-stamp — the measured one — and **not** the deliberate one. A manager stamping a live worker's id inside that worker's own window is still undetected; closing that honestly needs a per-session credential this repo does not have. The gap is named in the output rather than implied away.

⚠️ **Deliberately not registered in `check_collapsed_states.py`**, with the reason stated in-module: that registry skips `f == prod_path`, so a single-file CI guard whose only reader is its own `check()` cannot satisfy its consumer check without inventing a consumer module to be consumed — the *"the only way to 'fix' it was to write worse code"* failure the registry records against its own earlier evidence model. The pattern is followed in full; the entry is not faked. If the registry grows a same-file consumer notion, this belongs in it.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — CI guard logic and registers only. No data schema, model boundary, pipeline stage, deployment stage, runtime responsibility, public API, inter-process contract, or configuration shape is touched.

## Test plan

- [x] `check_manager_scope.py --self-test`: **19 cases → 23**, all passing. The MI-106 pair is a **plant** (manager trailer, manager **not** in office, touching `src/` → `unattributed`, no finding, and the note must name the register) and a **control** (the **same diff** and the **same trailer** authored **inside** the window → still `violation`), so the plant cannot be satisfied by a guard that has merely stopped enforcing R2.
- [x] Two further controls: an **untimestamped register still grades on the trailer alone and says so** — breaking the lease file must not become the cheap way past R2 — and the standing disclosure is asserted present on a **clean** run, since a limit printed only on failures is a limit no reader of a green run ever sees.
- [x] All 19 pre-existing cases pass unchanged, including `210min since the previous heartbeat -> violation (R7 only)` and `handover after a long silence -> clean`.
- [x] Measured against the live instance in a clean worktree: `5504200c` now reads `⚠️ UNATTRIBUTED … the register CONTRADICTS the trailer` instead of two R2 findings.
- [x] `scripts/ci/run_guards.py`: **PASS 63 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 22** locally (`pytest`, `pyyaml` and `import-linter` installed first — a missing runner grades identically to a failing test, MI-110).
- [x] `check_collapsed_states.py` clean; `check_backlog_refs.py` clean; `check_pr_landing.py` → `declared_self_land`.
- [ ] CI green

## Filed for follow-ups

**#10895 is still red, on a second and different defect that the first was masking.** R7 fails `5244dafb` — the **manager's own merge commit** — for *"223 minutes since this manager's previous heartbeat"*. That number is an artifact: `heartbeat_cadence_gap` reads the previous heartbeat from `sha~1`, and on a merge commit the first parent is the **worker branch's** tip, so it compares against whatever stale lease blob that branch carried. The register reachable from that same commit holds same-holder heartbeats at `08:32:50Z` and `09:21:42Z` — a **49-minute** gap, inside the 90-minute TTL and near the repo's measured 30-minute median. **The manager was on cadence.**

Filed as `BL-20260904-MANAGER-SCOPE-R7-MEASURES-CADENCE-ALONG-THE-FIRST-PARENT-SO-A-MANAGER-MERGE-INTO-A-WORKER-BRANCH-READS-AS-A-LAPSE` rather than folded in here: it is a different rule (R7, not R2) reached by a different mechanism (parent traversal, not authorship), and it is adjacent to **MI-105** — R6 and range membership — which already has an owner on this same guard. Folding it in would put two unrelated judgement changes behind one review.

⚠️ It is **invisible from #10895's own tree**, whose guard revision predates R7 entirely (0 occurrences), and shows up only under `main`'s guard — which is what CI runs, since `actions/checkout` resolves a `pull_request` event to the merge ref. Anyone re-measuring by checking out the PR head alone will see a false negative.

The standing do-nots for #10895 are unchanged and still correct: no manager-scope exception (it is not a live incident), no rewriting another session's commit, no merging past a failing required check. The cheaper instance-only route — `session_018ruZdgEkPZ1XceWzLwuYUU` re-committing under its own trailer — would have fixed the **instance** and left the evasion open; it is now moot for R2 and would not clear R7 either.
